project.topic: What if 8.3 billion people on Earth clapped at the same time?
project.title: What if 8.3 billion people on Earth clapped at the same time?
project.audience: Curious international viewers who enjoy surprising physical thought experiments.
project.core_question: Would one simultaneous worldwide clap reach your ears as one giant bang?
project.viewer_takeaway: 8.3 billion people means16.6 billion hands, but sound reaches each listener at different times. At343m/s a1km path takes2.92s; distance and reflections shape local applause.

captions.style: Inter Bold uppercase impact phrases with dark outline and shadow, 2-5 words, max two balanced lines
captions.active_word_treatment: Active word in solar yellow #FACC15 with a subtle scale lift.
captions.highlights_policy: The physical consequence of each scene in accent colour; at most two emphasis phrases per scene.

audio.voice_style: Crisp, urgent, fascinated adult male; high-tension simulation narrator; brisk opening cadence
audio.music_direction: Original restrained curious plucks; brief acoustic dip before the opening real handclap; ease the score during travel and echo evidence.
audio.sfx_direction: Actual recorded CC0 handclaps aligned to palm contact and selected-source arrivals. Quiet recorded park birds. One clap per person, replayed from explicit alternate views; no invented global sonic boom.

scientific_model.baseline_reality: Handclaps launch transient acoustic pressure disturbances. Sound travels at finite speed; geometric spreading and reflections shape what a listener hears.
scientific_model.counterfactual_change: Exactly the stipulated8.3 billion people each clap once at the same global instant.
assumptions: Participant count is stipulated, not a live census claim.
All participants make one ordinary clap; representative actors do not stand in for a literal rendered global population.
The film explicitly replays the same event from local perspectives and slow-motion explanation; replays are not additional human claps.
Still near20C air, modeled sound speed343m/s. Distances are selected examples; weather, barriers and absorption alter real propagation.
The1km result is travel time, not a guarantee that an individual handclap is audible at1km. Audio demonstrates selected source paths qualitatively, without a calibrated whole-city sound field.
Six-decibel reduction applies approximately to one ideal isolated free-field source per doubling of distance, with reflections excluded; it is not a measured worldwide level.
The chosen alley wall is30m from the source/listener, giving approximately60m roundtrip and0.175s reflected delay. Its gain is illustrative.
No universal peak decibel level, hearing outcome, destructive wave or earth movement is predicted.
causal_chain: One simultaneous contact per person involves16.6 billion hands.
Claps create pressure pulses; nearest direct sounds arrive first.
A selected1km air path takes1000/343=2.915s even though source hands have already separated.
Listeners at different positions receive different contributions and arrival times.
Free-field spreading weakens an isolated source about6dB per distance doubling.
Walls reflect existing sound, producing an encore without another human clap.
uncertainties: Actual clap spectra and loudness vary with hands and motion.
Source density, buildings, terrain, weather and background noise prevent one universal local sound level.
Visible thin acoustic paths/rings illustrate propagation; they are not visible air walls or a solved fluid field.

claims.statement: 8.3 billion people clapping once use16.6 billion hands; a handclap launches an acoustic pressure pulse.
claims.reasoning: 2 hands per participant; primary handclap experiments establish acoustic mechanisms.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Ordinary clap once, no global sound-energy sum.

claims.statement: A1km sound path takes about2.92s at the chosen343m/s.
claims.reasoning: t=distance/speed; sound speed follows air temperature.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Same-clap replay and local elapsed clock; no promise of distant audibility.

claims.statement: Without reflections, an ideal isolated source drops about6dB per distance doubling.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Explicitly exclude reflections; no summed global decibel claim.

claims.statement: Nearby walls can return a clap after the hands stop.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Reflection is the same pulse, not a second human clap.

sources.name: NASA Glenn: sound speed in air

creative_direction.logline: One perfect global clap becomes a different local listening experience, ending with an encore from a wall.
creative_direction.visual_identity: Bright textured city and open park; finite hand contact, same-event listening replays and boxless upper-left numerical readouts.
creative_direction.lighting: Warm directional daylight, blue sky fill, readable palm silhouettes and grounded shadows; quiet sky behind the number block.
creative_direction.camera_language: Eye-level palm contact, representative crowd reveal, same-pulse slow-motion and measured street-scale travel, then a grounded wall reflection callback.
creative_direction.motion_language: One finite clap per actor in each explicit replay; hands separate and settle. Thin acoustic markers trace selected paths with no destructive motion.
creative_direction.world_scale_policy: Metres.1000m selected source path;2m/4m free-field comparison;30m reflection wall. Sound markers are explanatory paths, not visible air shocks.
creative_direction.opening_hook: You clap once, yet applause keeps arriving after hands stop.
creative_direction.mid_video_rehook: A simultaneous source moment does not produce simultaneous arrivals; the selected distant crowd is already resting.
creative_direction.ending_payoff: A wall returns an encore even though nobody claps again.
creative_direction.loop_connection: Return to the opening character with still hands, looking toward the wall that supplies the last clap.
creative_direction.asset_policy: Reuse registered city, sky, Humanoid, grounded motion, sound rings and editorial HUD; add real CC0 clap and park recordings after source inspection.

distribution.primary_search_intent: What if 8.3 billion people on Earth clapped at the same time?
distribution.distinctive_angle: Top-left numbers track worldwide hands and local sound travel, while visibly resting hands expose the delay and a wall supplies the encore.
distribution.comment_bait_question: Would you hear it from a crowded square or a quiet hillside?
distribution.seo_integrity_note: Acoustics and physics qualifiers; no global sonic-boom or universal decibel claims.

asset_plan.library_snapshot_note: Inspected actual city, sky, Humanoid/grounded motion, acoustic rings and HUD. No recorded handclap existed; acquired and measured actual CC0 clips.
